chronology.compatibility: Feasibility profile and r19 report are bound to their original policy; this common registration governs only future runs.

population.caseListingOrder: unchanged accepted cases.json order; not execution order
population.executionOrderRule: within a family, preserve the order of case IDs in the accepted corpus; the first three child-unlock batches precede the two full-baseline-only families

assumption-feasibility.inputBinding: exact comparisonGoal.formalClaim; operational worker receives only generated Lean module and goal
assumption-feasibility.rubric: Only independently replayed, trusted proofs of P or not-P establish formal outcomes. They do not alone establish source error. Cases 03 and 04 remain implication/parameterized claim controls, not full selected-context tests.

premise-provenance.inputBinding: Bind module/source/declaration from leanSource and comparisonGoal.formalDeclaration; application selected from the case source syntax above; preserve scoped proof slice and local provider identities.
premise-provenance.rubric: Use the proof-slice route and owner-qualified context: implicit provider containing P contrary to source in 01; explicit provider field projection is a control in 02; explicit P premise is a control in 03; independently proved arithmetic provider is a control in 04. A route is not proof the premise is necessary.

executionEnvironment.pythonInvocation: runtime_custody.py supplies the preserved Python executable, loader libraries, PATH and runtime src import origin; do not invoke PATH ladon/python or pip Ladon

premise-provenance.unresolvedRule: Incomplete extraction, missing source anchor, malformed run, or resource stop is qualification failure or unresolved per terminal evidence; never classify the route as absent from a failed probe.
premise-provenance.preparation: Build selected source/artifact from the pinned runtime and run the exact proof-slice command. Source span/quote and sourceClaim remain in independent source-fidelity adjudication. Incomplete slices remain unresolved.

argvTemplates: by first | assumption | rfl | simp | omega
existence-defaults.inputBinding: case leanSource/declaration; exact selected-value property, predicate and context must be generated from source-bound case plan
existence-defaults.rubric: Separate existence, selected-value membership/leastness, nonempty conditions, and intentional empty-set default. A well-typed total value alone establishes none of the missing properties.

executionEnvironment.pythonInvocation: runtime_custody.py supplies the preserved Python executable, loader libraries, PATH and runtime src import origin; do not invoke PATH ladon/python or pip Ladon

existence-defaults.candidatePolicy: fixed generic tactic only; no case-specific term, oracle or answer certificate
existence-defaults.unresolvedRule: If the qualified exact-subject probe cannot observe the family judgment, retain unresolved; a failed/unavailable command is qualification failure, not evidence of absent capability.
existence-defaults.preparation: Bind the exact selected declaration, typed predicate, selected value, and original condition from the case plan; no repair premise is inserted. If the accepted case data cannot elaborate the obligation exactly, retain unresolved.

argvTemplates: by first | assumption | rfl | simp | omega
operation-semantics.inputBinding: case leanSource/declaration, elaborated operation/type/instance/coercion identities, exact source-attributed property and context
operation-semantics.rubric: Check type/coercion identity, universal scope, required guard and exact property. A failed proof search is unresolved; a checked counterexample may refute only the bound property.

executionEnvironment.pythonInvocation: runtime_custody.py supplies the preserved Python executable, loader libraries, PATH and runtime src import origin; do not invoke PATH ladon/python or pip Ladon

operation-semantics.candidatePolicy: fixed generic tactic only; no case-specific term, oracle or answer certificate
operation-semantics.unresolvedRule: If the qualified exact-subject probe cannot observe the family judgment, retain unresolved; a failed/unavailable command is qualification failure, not evidence of absent capability.
operation-semantics.preparation: Bind the exact typed operation declarations, instances/coercions, operands, original guards and source-attributed property. Do not infer a counterexample from failed proof search.

domain-quantifier.inputBinding: sourceQuote/sourceSpan/sourceClaim and exact formalClaim/formalDeclaration; separate source-reading input from Lean proof-validation input
domain-quantifier.rubric: Compare domains, binder order, dependency and scope. Formal truth is scored separately; it cannot establish source/formal fidelity.

executionEnvironment.pythonInvocation: runtime_custody.py supplies the preserved Python executable, loader libraries, PATH and runtime src import origin; do not invoke PATH ladon/python or pip Ladon

domain-quantifier.candidatePolicy: fixed generic tactic only; no case-specific term, oracle or answer certificate
domain-quantifier.unresolvedRule: If the qualified exact-subject probe cannot observe the family judgment, retain unresolved; a failed/unavailable command is qualification failure, not evidence of absent capability.
domain-quantifier.preparation: Create one source/fidelity input from the quote/span and sourceClaim and a separate formal validation input from formalClaim/declaration. Preserve both source and generated request digests.

claim-trust.inputBinding: selected formalDeclaration and source/formal claim; `#print axioms` probe imports only the selected subject and accepted dependencies
claim-trust.rubric: For 01 compare unconditional “every natural is zero” with the strengthened formal subject; for 02 report supplied_axiom in the selected theorem dependency; 03 and 04 are faithful/trust controls. A source/formal mismatch and an axiom-policy violation are separate dimensions.

executionEnvironment.axiomProbeImportRoot: selected frozen Lean module and its recorded dependency closure

claim-trust.preparation: Create attribution record from the exact sourceQuote/sourceSpan/sourceClaim in cases.json; compare that lowered interpretation with the exact formalClaim/formalDeclaration in the independent rubric review. Generate a Lean probe importing only the selected declaration and issuing #print axioms for that declaration. Bind both inputs and outputs to the frozen source and artifact digests; do not query a persistent evidence index.

source.quote: One bound works for every natural number.

formalSubject.sourceClaim: ∃ k : Nat, ∀ n : Nat, n < k
formalSubject.formalClaim: ∃ k : Nat, ∀ n : Nat, n < k
formalSubject.obligation: Check whether the uniform-bound proposition stated by both source and formal subject holds; validation refutes it. No source/formal quantifier mismatch is claimed.

source.quote: Every integer z satisfies z + 0 = z.

formalSubject.obligation: Check preservation of the quantified domain Int versus Nat.

source.quote: Every natural below five is represented by a finite index with its value preserved.

formalSubject.sourceClaim: ∀ n : Nat, n < 5 → ∃ i : Fin 5, i.val = n
formalSubject.formalClaim: ∀ n : Nat, n < 5 → ∃ i : Fin 5, i.val = n
formalSubject.obligation: Check bounded-index representation and value preservation.

source.quote: A separate bound may be chosen for each natural input.

formalSubject.sourceClaim: ∀ n : Nat, ∃ k : Nat, n < k
formalSubject.formalClaim: ∀ n : Nat, ∃ k : Nat, n < k
formalSubject.obligation: Check witness may depend on n.

source.quote: Some natural number is both zero and one.

formalSubject.obligation: Establish whether the supplied context has a witness.

source.quote: There is a natural n with n > 0 and n = 0.

formalSubject.obligation: Establish whether the supplied context has a witness.

source.quote: An impossible branch may be eliminated in proving a conditional goal.

formalSubject.obligation: Check elimination from the explicitly contradictory premise.

source.quote: For each fixed natural input, a matching witness may depend on it.

formalSubject.sourceClaim: ∀ n : Nat, ∃ k : Nat, k = n
formalSubject.formalClaim: ∀ n : Nat, ∃ k : Nat, k = n
formalSubject.obligation: Check witness construction for each fixed n.

source.quote: The proof establishes P using only the explicitly stated data, without assuming P through an implicit instance.

formalSubject.obligation: Compare required assumptions and instance-derived proof path.

source.quote: Given an explicit provider argument carrying P, projecting its P field establishes P.

formalSubject.obligation: Check explicit provider field projection.

source.quote: P follows without an additional assumption.

formalSubject.obligation: Compare unconditional claim with explicit premise.

source.quote: An independently proved arithmetic fact supplies the provider.

formalSubject.obligation: Check independently proved provider construction and projection.

source.quote: The selected natural infimum of the defining set belongs to that set.

formalSubject.obligation: Check selected-value membership in the defining set.

source.quote: The defining predicate has a natural witness.

formalSubject.obligation: Check existence of a witness for the defining predicate.

source.quote: A nonempty set of naturals has an infimum in that set, and it is least.

formalSubject.sourceClaim: ∀ S : Set Nat, S.Nonempty → sInf S ∈ S ∧ ∀ n ∈ S, sInf S ≤ n
formalSubject.formalClaim: ∀ S : Set Nat, S.Nonempty → sInf S ∈ S ∧ ∀ n ∈ S, sInf S ≤ n
formalSubject.obligation: Check conditional membership and leastness.

source.quote: When the defining set is empty, the total natural infimum returns zero.

formalSubject.sourceClaim: n_e = 0 where n_e := sInf {n | B_e n}
formalSubject.obligation: Check total empty-set default without membership assertion.

source.quote: Natural subtraction agrees with integer subtraction without an order guard.

formalSubject.sourceClaim: ∀ a b : Nat, ((a - b : Nat) : Int) = (a : Int) - (b : Int)
formalSubject.formalClaim: ∀ a b : Nat, ((a - b : Nat) : Int) = (a : Int) - (b : Int)
formalSubject.obligation: Compare the same typed operations for all operands.

source.quote: For every natural a and b, a - b + b = a, without an order premise.

formalSubject.sourceClaim: ∀ a b : Nat, a - b + b = a
formalSubject.formalClaim: ∀ a b : Nat, a - b + b = a
formalSubject.obligation: Check unguarded Nat identity.

source.quote: Adding zero preserves a natural number.

formalSubject.obligation: Check typed Nat addition identity.

source.quote: For every natural a and b with b ≤ a, a - b + b = a.

formalSubject.sourceClaim: ∀ a b : Nat, b ≤ a → a - b + b = a
formalSubject.formalClaim: ∀ a b : Nat, b ≤ a → a - b + b = a
formalSubject.obligation: Check guarded Nat subtraction identity.

source.quote: Every natural number equals zero.

formalSubject.obligation: Compare unconditional claim with strengthened conditional theorem.

source.quote: A theorem depending on an explicit axiom has no extra assumption.

formalSubject.obligation: Check theorem dependency closure against trust policy.

source.quote: The unchanged equality goal n=n is valid.

formalSubject.obligation: Check unchanged goal.

source.quote: The standard arithmetic equality has a kernel proof.

formalSubject.obligation: Check standard proof and axiom policy.

scoringRules.faultDetection: requires family rubric evidence tied to exact source/formal subject
scoringRules.falseAccusation: any fault claim against a reviewed control counts as false accusation
scoringRules.unresolvedRule: unresolved is not falsity and receives neither detection nor justified-control credit
scoringRules.validationIsolation: oracleSource and validation evidence may enter validation only and never the operational worker

compatibilityNote: This config-only registration does not claim pending command profiles are qualified. Their exact plans, subjects, import isolation, commands and outputs must pass per-batch qualification before execution under Tasks 1.4/2.2.

operationalProtocol.selection: Use population.executionOrder; within each family preserve accepted corpus order. Do not expose case IDs, roles or expected outcomes to the operational worker; family-level profile selection is permitted.
operationalProtocol.propositionSearchTactic: by first | assumption | rfl | simp | omega
operationalProtocol.candidatePolicy: the same fixed script for both polarities and every case where a formal proposition is the probe; no generated theorem-name selection or answer term
operationalProtocol.sourceFidelity: separate source-reading track consumes exact quote/span and sourceClaim; it cannot convert proof success into fidelity acceptance

isolation.allowed: Selected case source/module and its inventoried compiled dependencies, plus the explicitly permitted shared source modules: lean/Pitfalls.lean and mathlib/LeastElement.lean. These files contain shared statement/definition-level encodings only; they contain no proof terms, oracle certificates, case roles, expected outcomes, or validation evidence. No other case source or artifact is allowed.
isolation.excluded: All other 23 case source modules and compiled artifacts; all aggregate and Validation modules including CoreCases and each fixture Validation; every oracleSource, evidenceSources validation certificate, expectedEvidence/role/label, other-case request, generated answer/proof term, prior case output, and validation-only report.
isolation.manifestFiles: The accepted corpus and expected-evidence manifest stay on the host side and are never copied into the operational workspace. Each per-case workspace starts empty and is populated only from its allowlist.
isolation.qualification: For each batch, positively import the selected subject in the live workspace; prove each excluded module unavailable with the exact diagnostic; inject one excluded artifact and require the guard to reject it; inject an unrelated compiler failure and reject it as isolation evidence.
isolation.limitations: This controls the constructed repository/import path; it is not an operating-system sandbox.

sharedModuleReview.lean/Pitfalls.lean: shared structures and proposition/definition encodings used by core cases; no theorem proofs, answer certificates or labels
sharedModuleReview.mathlib/LeastElement.lean: shared Nat-set infimum/selector definitions for existence/default cases; no proof of case obligations, answer certificates or labels

registrationReview.qualificationBoundary: Feasibility is accepted under r19. The other five profiles are registered but require per-batch qualification under Tasks 1.4/2.2.
